why: A 2026 arXiv paper 'On Brocard's problem with Padovan and Perrin numbers' proves (n,x)=(4,5) is the only solution when x is restricted to being a Padovan or Perrin number, which may be a genuine restricted case of this exact equation rather than a different problem; separately, Wataru Takeda solved only the polynomial analogue (a different, changed problem, not counted), and the integer problem remains otherwise unproven with no new unconditional result found.

found.title: On Brocard's problem with Padovan and Perrin numbers
found.note: Claims (n,x)=(4,5) is the only solution to n!+1=x^2 when x is a Padovan or Perrin number; a restricted-case result on the same equation, not read in full.

found.title: A Problem Proposed in 1876 Just Got Its First Real Breakthrough
found.note: Reports Wataru Takeda solved the polynomial analogue of the Brocard-Ramanujan problem, explicitly not the integer version Wikipedia states.

found.title: The Brocard Problem: Structural Invariants, p-Adic Density, and the Generative Sieve
found.note: Proposes a reformulation and sieve algorithm for searching solutions; does not claim resolution.
